speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Well count me out.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: What? Why?

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: You want me to use my intelligence in a tawdry competition? Would you ask Picasso to play Pictionary? Would you ask Noah Webster to play Boggle? Would you ask Jacques Cousteau to play Go Fish?

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Come on, you need a four person team, we're four people.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: By that reasoning we should also play bridge, hold up a chuppah and enter the Olympic bobsled competition.

speaker: penny
text: I want tickets to that please.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: Sheldon, what, do I need to quote Spock's dying words to you.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: No, don't.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: The needs of the many.

speaker: howard_wolowitz
text: Outweigh the needs of the few.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Or the one. Dammit, I'll do it.

speaker: raj_koothrappali
text: Okay. First order of physics bowl business. We need a truly kick- ass team name. Suggestions.

speaker: howard_wolowitz
text: How about the perpetual motion squad? It's beyond the laws of physics, plus a little heads up for the ladies.

speaker: leonard_hofstadter
text: The ladies?

speaker: howard_wolowitz
text: Perpetual motion squad, we can go all night.

speaker: raj_koothrappali
text: I like it.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I don't. Teams are traditionally named after fierce creatures, thus intimidating ones opponent.

speaker: raj_koothrappali
text: Then we can be the Bengal Tigers.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Poor choice. Gram for gram, no animal exceeds the relative fighting strength of the army ant.

speaker: raj_koothrappali
text: Maybe so. But you can't incinerate a Bengal Tiger with a magnifying glass.
